doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bands on the Weinberg southern tour
summary: Many big bands passed through Greensboro on a Weinberg-booked circuit of dance halls from New York to Florida.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What other bands came through Greensboro?

Oh, man, all of them came through there. Jay McShann. Andy Kirk. Erskine Hawkins. Lionel Hampton, of course. Illinois Jacquet, of course. Illinois Jacquet, of course. Louis Jordan. Several other bands—I can’t think of all of them.
So this was all during that year or two after you were discharged from the Navy.
They were all coming through Greensboro on their southern tours.
Yeah. They had 60 one-nighters from New York to Florida.
Who did? Each of the different bands...

No, it was a tour down there they called the Weinberg Tour. A guy named Weinberg used to book them. He bought all the dance halls from New York to Florida, and he’d send the bands down there, and they played. Dizzy’s band came through there.
What did the Mombassa Club look like? How was it set up?
Ah, just a club. Kind of dark in there. It was an exotic looking club. Heh-heh. For the South.
